detail: All are curated rows. A licence name alone does not let a user verify a number, and the spec's rule is not to hide the source.
Legitimate for water, black coffee, most spices in trace amounts. Listed because zero and 'not recorded' are indistinguishable in this schema, so the count is an upper bound on genuine zeroes.
spec_reference: master:never replace missing values with zero

detail: last_verified_at is NULL on every row, by design: a non-constant column default would have forced a full rewrite of 578,773 rows. It means no row can currently be shown as stale.

Nutrition is inline, single-valued and per-row. Provenance is attached to the ROW, not to each nutrient value. A re-import therefore overwrites history irrecoverably. Count is 0 because this is a schema property, not a row defect; severity is unrelated to the count.

565,814 rows are Open Food Facts under ODbL. Share-alike and attribution obligations bind any export, redistribution or derived-data feature. Not a data defect; a constraint that must be settled before an export feature is designed.
finding: ODbL obligations on 97.8 percent of rows

detail: Exceeds the energy density of pure fat (~900 kcal/100 g). Oils sit legitimately near the bound; values materially above it are unit errors. Not repaired in Phase 0.
lang is the empty string on all rows. The column and its uniqueness constraint exist and are correct; nothing populates them. Multilingual search is structurally present and functionally absent.
finding: Language tag empty on every alias row

detail: calories > 0 while protein_g, carbs_g and fat_g are all 0. Macro-energy consistency cannot hold. Distinguishing 'genuinely zero' from 'not recorded' is impossible because the schema has no null-vs-zero distinction for macros.
finding: Positive energy with all macronutrients zero
spec_reference: master:macro-energy consistency; master:never replace missing with zero

detail: Groups sharing name_normalized. Not necessarily defects: Open Food Facts legitimately holds one product name across brands, markets and formulations. The schema cannot express that distinction today, so de-duplication and market variance are one unsolved problem.

Every value is 'per 100 g' with no basis column. Raw, cooked, drained, as-prepared and dry-matter bases cannot be distinguished. The only machinery that exists reads preparation_key out of the names_i18n JSONB blob, where it cannot be indexed or constrained.
No table and no column. The spec forbids inferring safety from a food name, so nothing can be derived from what is present. Safety-critical.
Rows with an empty serving_sizes array. All are USDA-sourced. A per-100 g value with no household portion cannot be logged by a user without an invented conversion.

98.7 percent of the catalogue carries neither. Of those that do, 7,087 are the catch-all 'global'. A single flat text column also cannot express the hierarchical, multi-association taxonomy the spec requires.
names_i18n is populated on 347 of 578,773 rows. No row anywhere holds a native-script name, which is why Indic, Cyrillic and CJK queries return zero results.
Distinct rows normalising to the same GTIN-14. Small enough to review by hand. A barcode should identify one trade item.
